_doc: Sutton, Braxton County, West Virginia, February 1994: the Office hub. One short block of Main Street on the Elk River below Sutton Dam. The Office is the old post office; its rooms open onto the back lane behind it (vault, darkroom, lab, loading dock, radio shack, bunk room). The map has a void border and no exits: the road out is the station wagon on the lane. Positions are in 32px tiles.
name: Sutton

facades.name: Dodrill Pawn & Loan
facades.locked: BACK AT 2. It is a quarter past three and the sign has said that since Christmas.

facades.name: The dead letter vault
facades.locked: Sealed since 1953. The key is not in the Office.

look: The payphone outside McKee's. It rings some nights. Dot says don't answer it.

props.name: The flagpole
look: The Office flag. Forty-eight stars. Nobody has told it.
Gus bought it in 1953. Dot won't replace a thing that still works.

props.look: The Office's own box. LAST COLLECTION 4:30. Dot empties it at 4:29 so the Post Office never gets a chance.
The diner's bin, on the side road. Coffee grounds, a Braxton Democrat, and a ticket for a sixteen-ounce T-bone, paid in dimes.

props.name: Newspaper box
look: The Braxton Democrat, weekly. 'DAM RELEASE SCHEDULE CHANGED.' Page one. Page one is the only page.
Below the fold: coyote took a goat at Heaters. That's news.

props.look: A bench outside the pawn shop. Somebody waits on it for the shop to open, every day, and it never does.

look: County plough truck. The blade is up and the bed is full of salt and one deer, dressed.
That's Hollis's. The deer is legal. Mostly.
Dark sedan outside the Office. Plates from Kanawha County. Engine cold.
It's the dam engineer's, June. He's in the diner.

props.look: Pearl Dodrill's Buick. She has driven it to the diner every morning since 1971. The diner is two hundred feet from her house.

props.name: Highway sign
look: ROUTE 4. GASSAWAY 9. FLATWOODS 6. Under FLATWOODS somebody painted a small green man. Somebody else painted him out. He's back.
Six miles. We drive past that turnoff every time.
And we will keep driving past it, dear, until Dot says otherwise.

props.look: A bench facing the river. The plaque reads FOR A. W., WHO LISTENED. No date, because nobody agreed on one.

look: A snowman in an Office trench coat. The coat is ours.
Redbone hound. Belongs to the dam crew. Walks the whole river twice a day and reports to nobody.

props.look: A johnboat frozen into the bank. Somebody shovelled it out as far as the oarlocks and thought better of it.

props.name: Sutton Dam overlook
look: The dam fills the end of the river like a wall somebody forgot to finish. The Corps of Engineers marker says 1961. The spillway hums.
It's a tone under the spillway. I'll log it.

props.look: A bicycle against the darkroom wall. Both reflectors on. Teddy checked.
The darkroom bin. Fixer bottles and one print, torn in four. It's a photograph of the sky over the dam. Nothing in it. That's why it's torn.

props.name: The station wagon
look: The Office's station wagon. Three hundred thousand miles, a heater that works on Tuesdays, and Ruth's casserole dish still in the back.
The dish is clean. The car is not.

props.look: Gas cans by the dock door. Two full, one empty, one that says WATER in Dot's hand and is not water.

props.name: The mast
look: The mast. Twenty feet of pipe, guyed to a fence post and a fifty-five Chevy that isn't going anywhere.
It works. Don't touch the Chevy.

props.name: Brass plate
look: A brass plate screwed to the stair door: DEAD LETTERS. SEALED 1953. The screws are newer than the plate.

props.name: The pigeonholes
look: Forty pigeonholes, one per county, and nine more Dot added for states. Mason County's is full. Braxton's is empty. Braxton always is.
Nobody writes to the Office about their own town.
A Royal. Dot types every reply on it, two fingers, no mistakes. The ribbon is older than June.

props.name: The Office ledger
props.look: The Office ledger, 1953 to now. Budget in on the left page, budget out on the right. The right page is longer.

look: The Office phone. SUTTON 765-2211. One line. Ruth is usually on it.

props.look: The mail cart. Today's letters, sorted by Dot into NOW, SOON, and a third pile she calls LORD.

props.name: Gus Weller's calendar
look: A feed-store calendar. December 1967. The 15th is circled. Nothing after it is written on, and nobody has turned the page.

props.name: The card catalog
look: Oak, thirty-six drawers, A to Z and ten more. Every case the Office ever filed, one card each. Drawer S has a lock on it and the lock is not oak.
WELLER, A. PERSONAL, in Dot's hand. The drawer is empty except for a pair of reading glasses and a receipt from the Lowe Hotel, Point Pleasant, December 1967.
She meant to come back for the glasses.

props.name: Gus Weller's desk
look: The founder's desk. Blotter, inkwell, a brass lamp, and her trench coat still over the back of the chair as if she stepped out to the diner.
Dot has never let anyone sit there. Including Dot.

props.name: The wall of photographs
look: Framed photographs, 1953 to 1993. Every team the Office ever sent out, standing by the wagon. The first one is two people. The woman is laughing. The man is not.
That's Penrose. He hasn't aged a day in forty years and he's not in any photo after '67.

props.name: The case board
props.look: The sorting-room board. Red string, index cards, and one map pin pushed so hard it has gone through the cork into the wall.

look: The sorting table. Letters from the public in three heaps: BIRD, LIGHTS, and OTHER. OTHER is the tallest.
Half of BIRD is OTHER. They just don't know it yet.

props.name: Dead letter tray
props.look: The tray for letters the Office cannot answer. Dot takes it down to the vault door once a month and leaves it there. In the morning it is empty.
Plumbing, electrical, and a hand-lettered shelf of LANTERN MANTLES, BATTERIES, FILM, PLASTER. McKee calls it the Office shelf and stocks it on Mondays.

look: Traps, snare wire, a cast of a bear track McKee made himself and priced at forty dollars.

props.look: A Snap-on calendar. February 1994, the right month, the right year. The only correct calendar in Sutton.

look: Rock salt by the hundredweight. For the walk, McKee says. He does not ask what we do with it.

props.name: The order book
props.look: McKee's order book, open. Last line, in Dot's hand: 'Plaster, 2 bags. Charge the Office. Don't argue.'
The key-cutting bench. A board of blanks, and one hook labelled OFFICE BASEMENT with no key on it. McKee says there never was one.
Chain, by the foot. McKee sells it to the Office in ten-foot lengths and never asks why it comes back shorter.

look: Beagle. Asleep on the chain. Nobody's stolen a foot of it in thirty years.

props.look: The sink. A radio on the sill tuned to WDBS in Sutton. It plays bluegrass and the dam release times, and the dam release times are the part people listen to.

look: Two pots. One says REGULAR. One says DAM CREW and is black as the spillway.
Ruth drinks the dam crew one.
Apple, buttermilk, and a sign that says NO MOTHMAN JOKES. Somebody has crossed out MOTHMAN and written FLATWOODS.
The sign is older than the joke.

props.name: Corkboard
props.look: The corkboard. Dam release times. A flyer for the Braxton County Monster Festival, 1993, with the monster drawn by a child. Under it, in Dot's hand: 'Office is next door. Letters only. No walk-ins.' Below that: 'Walk-ins fine. Dot.'

look: Ralph Stanley, three times. Somebody with quarters and one opinion.

props.look: A framed photograph of the dam going up, 1960. The river behind it is in the wrong place, because they moved it.
The last stool is Hollis Bragg's. Nobody else sits on it, not because of Hollis. Because of the stool. It rocks.

look: Pearl Dodrill's booth. The seat is worn to the frame on one side. The other side has a Gideon Bible, a crossword and a photograph face down.
Leave it face down, dear. She'll turn it over when she's ready.

props.look: The kitchen bin. Eggshells, a Democrat, and a bus ticket, Gassaway to Charleston, unused. Somebody keeps meaning to.

props.name: The upgrade bench
look: The dock bench. A CB radio still in the box, a spotlight bracket, and a drawing of a mattress in the back of the wagon with measurements in June's hand.

props.look: A workshop table and the wagon's shop manual, 1978, open to HEATER. The page is black with thumbprints and the heater still works on Tuesdays.
Oil, belts, bulbs, and a coffee can of fuses marked DON'T, in Gus Weller's hand. The fuses are fine. Nobody uses them.
A tyre-shop calendar, 1986. The month is right. The year is a long story.

look: Thirty gallons of gas. Rationed by Ruth.

props.name: The glovebox pile
props.look: Everything that has ever come out of the wagon's glovebox. Maps of four states, a harmonica, a 1967 parking stub from the Lowe Hotel, Point Pleasant. Nobody has claimed the harmonica.
A ladder to the loft. The loft is where the radio shack's cables go and where Teddy says he will sleep if June plays the tone again.

props.name: The enlarger
look: A Beseler enlarger, 1950s, in a room that was built for it. Dot said the first verdict buys the bulb. It did.

props.name: The trays
props.look: Developer, stop, fix, in three trays. The tongs are labelled in Gus Weller's hand, DEV, STOP, FIX, and a fourth pair, labelled DON'T.

look: The safelight. Red. It has been red since 1953 and it makes everyone look like they have been crying.

props.name: The drying line
props.look: Prints on a line. Mason Gas sign, the church fence, the Lowe Hotel. One is blank. It was not blank when it went up.

look: A camera bag. Not ours. A Leica, 1960s, and a roll of film still in it, exposed, never developed. The tag says A. W., DEC 67.
We develop it. We develop it tonight.

props.name: The negatives
props.look: A box of negative sleeves, 1953 to 1967, each labelled in a tall slanting hand. 1967 ends in December. The last sleeve is empty.

props.name: The spectrometer
look: A bench spectrometer. Surplus, 1971, and it was surplus then. It tells the truth, which is more than I can say for the witnesses.

props.name: The bench
props.look: The old parcel-room bench. The scale is still bolted to it. Dot weighs the evidence on it. Literally.

look: Reagents. And one jar labelled TNT AREA WATER, DO NOT DRINK, which was two dollars at Harmon's and is worth every cent.

props.look: Lab results, by case. The oldest folder is marked FLATWOODS 1952, and it has one page in it, and the page says SEE DRAWER S.

props.name: The sample case
look: Gus Weller's sample case. Leather, brass corners, her initials. Inside: twelve numbered vials, eleven empty. The twelfth is sealed with wax and has no number.

props.name: The rig
look: A Hallicrafters, a Drake, and whatever I built in between. It hears the dam, the state police, and once, in November, something that answered.

props.name: The station log
props.look: The station log. Every frequency the Office has heard since 1953, by hand. The first entry is Gus Weller's: 'Three notes, 0210. Not the dam.'

look: The scanner. Police, fire, the Corps of Engineers. Mostly it's the dam telling itself what time it is.

props.look: Tapes, by year. The 1966 box is empty and a note in it says 'Walter has it.' The note is in pencil and the pencil is very hard.

props.name: June's parts box
look: June's parts box. Tubes, crystals, a soldering iron, and a photograph of a dog.
A shared dresser. Top drawer, Miriam, labelled. Second, Teddy, not labelled, not closed. Third, nobody's, with one wool trench coat folded in it, 1950s cut, A. W. in the collar.

props.look: A photograph pinned above the beds. The team at the Elk Diner, last Christmas. Elijah is the only one looking at the camera, and he is not looking at the camera.

look: My books. Please do not alphabetise them again, Miriam.

props.look: February 1994. Dot's calendar. Every day the wagon is out is marked with a small careful x, and today is not marked yet.

look: Teddy's bunk. Notebook under the pillow, a Register under the mattress, and a pie plate from the Elk under the bed.

props.look: Ruth's bed. Quilt, Bible, and a casserole dish on the nightstand that is not the one in the wagon. There are more.

props.name: June's footlocker
look: A footlocker, padlocked. Taped to the lid: DO NOT OPEN. TUNED.

props.look: A Scrabble box. Elijah is banned from playing. Not for cheating. For knowing.
